newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln National Q1 annuity earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln National Q1 annuity earnings up.

text.p: Lincoln National Corp on Tuesday said its life insurance and annuities segment produced first-quarter operating income of more than $76 million, up 17 percent from the same period a year ago.
Lincoln National said annuity earnings led the way, rising 37 percent to $47 million from $34.4 million.
But Lincoln National's U.S. life insurance operations produced operating income of $10.2 million in the first quarter, down from $11.3 million in the year-earlier period.
The decline was the result of an unusually large number of high-dollar claims, the company said.
The company reported overall operating earnings of $1.14 a share compared with $0.91 a year ago.
That topped analysts' First Call consensus estimate of $1.05 a share. Lincoln National shares were up one to 53-1/8 early Tuesday afternoon.
In annuities, Lincoln National said fixed and variable annuity account values rose 23 percent to $38.9 billion.

Annuity deposits of $1.0 billion were down 10 percent from a strong first quarter of 1996, with deposits up 21 percent from the agent distribution channel and down 30 percent from the stockbroker channel, the company said.
Variable annuity product enhancements are scheduled to be introduced in May and are expected to increase deposits, the company said.
Lincoln National said 401(k) deposits of $178 million were down seven percent from the first quarter of 1996, while 401(k) account values increased 16 percent to $2.9 billion.
Lincoln(UK), Lincoln National's life insurance and pension affiliate in Britain, reported first-quarter operating income of $16.5 million, compared with $17.5 million in the same period last year.

Lincoln National said its investment management segment, primarily composed of Delaware Management Holdings, Lynch & Mayer and Vantage Global Advisors, posted first-quarter operating income of $500,000, down from $3.8 million.

The decline primarily reflected reduced earnings from Lynch & Mayer, which had a strong quarter in the year-earlier quarter, and costs related to retail mutual fund growth initiatives at Delaware, Lincoln National said.
Lincoln National, based in Fort Wayne, Indiana, offers annuities, life insurance, reinsurance, property-casualty insurance, mutual funds and investment management services.
